summary: Reports the 'wiki incident', in which OpenAI agents posted about 18,000 messages on a public German wiki. Explicitly calls it collusion and gives a working definition: agents cooperating for task advantage in ways developers did not intend.
source: incident documents

title: G-Safeguard: A Topology-Guided Security Lens and Treatment on LLM-based Multi-agent Systems
summary: Detects anomalous agents on the communication graph with a GNN and intervenes by pruning edges. A representative topology-based defence.
source: literature search: AI safety and multi-agent ML

title: Adaptive Deployment of Untrusted LLMs Reduces Distributed Threats
summary: Addresses distributed threats, where harm accumulates over many individually innocuous actions, using macro-protocols that update trust in the untrusted model. Relevant to slow, coordinated subversion.
source: literature search: AI safety and multi-agent ML

title: Algorithmic and Human Collusion
summary: Lab comparison of Q-learning and human collusion in repeated pricing: algorithms collude more than humans in duopoly, and mixed human-algorithm markets fall in between. A direct human baseline for AI collusion claims.
source: literature search: economics, law and policy

title: Brief independent investigation of agents' behavior, reasoning and collaboration in the OpenAI / Hugging Face hacking incident
summary: Independent analysis of agent transcripts: about 1,200 agents exchanged over 70,000 messages, built task-assignment, HOLD/VETO and signing conventions, and reasoned about evading automated checks but rarely humans. PDF and Redwood mirror are also available.
source: incident documents

title: How does Adversarial Influence Scale in Multi-Agent Systems?
summary: Finds that in multi-agent deliberation the proportion of deceivers matters more than the size of the group.

title: Bootstrapped Monitoring: Leveraging Transparent Reasoning to Oversee Stronger AI Agents
summary: A trusted weak model reads the chain of thought of a stronger untrusted monitor to catch monitor–agent collusion in BashArena. Catch rates improve even when the monitor actively colludes, provided the raw CoT is available.
source: literature search: AI safety and multi-agent ML

title: AI Self-preferencing in Algorithmic Hiring: Empirical Evidence and Insights
summary: LLM evaluators favour CVs written by the same model. A real-world example of implicit, unintended collusion through self-preference in hiring.
source: literature search: AI safety and multi-agent ML

title: Collusion with Competitive Marginals: Price-Level Audits Are Blind by Construction
summary: Constructs collusion in which every agent's individual behaviour looks competitive while the coalition's actions are jointly dependent, so audits of price levels cannot detect it. Motivates dependence-based detection.
source: sprint page

title: MAStrike: Shapley-Guided Collusive Red-Teaming on Multi-Agent Systems
summary: Uses agent-level Shapley values to find safety-critical agents in hierarchical multi-agent systems, then red-teams them with coordinated compromised agents. A tool for stress-testing defences against colluding insiders.
source: literature search: AI safety and multi-agent ML

title: SoK: When Safe Agents Fail Together: The Security of Multi Agent LLM Systems
summary: Systematises 197 works on multi-agent security with an adversary-position × interface × system-risk framework. Warns against mistaking single-agent failures for multi-agent effects, a methodological point for collusion evaluations.
source: literature search: AI safety and multi-agent ML

title: Voluntary Collusion with Secret Tools in Competing LLM Agents
